_comment: Every deliberate difference between a binding's public names and docs/reference/bindings-v1.md, each with its written reason. Read by scripts/parity-surface.py (the parity gate, public issue #436); CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Changing a public name' says when an entry belongs here and when the doc or the bindings should change instead.

kind 'extra': public names the doc does not give (globs allowed, in the binding's own spelling: Owner.member, Owner.method(kw=) for a Python keyword-only parameter). kind 'missing': names the doc gives that the binding lacks (the doc's spelling). kind 'spelling': the doc's name `doc` that the binding spells `as`.
An entry, or a name in one, that matches nothing fails the gate as stale: remove it with the difference it explained.
An entry that hides a real gap, not a deliberate difference, carries `issue`: the public issue its fix waits on. `parity-surface.py --check-issues` fails once that issue is closed.

entries.reason: CHS_EXPORT_NONE (-1), the description's export-off constant, typed Format so that WithExport(ExportNone) type-checks. Python and TypeScript spell it EXPORT_NONE at module level (their own entries), and Rust's `export: Option<Format>` says it with None. Not a format: the vocabulary check counts Format's members without it.

The named types WithColumns and WithSettings return: one value implements several option interfaces (§2's call options: WithSettings implements CompileOption, RowOption, RowsOption, BlockOption, FilterOption and EvalOption), which Go's functional options can only express with a named type. The other three bindings carry the same options as fields, so they have nothing to name.

§4's 'a cache fault' bullet: a CHTYPES_CACHE_UNUSABLE (fetch-v1.md §1, the cache faults; public issue #486) carries the path, the reason and the errno name, which the doc names in prose and does not spell per language. Go keeps the path and the reason on ArtifactError's Path and Reason, which a loader refusal also uses.

§6: the fetch options carry everything fetch-v1.md configures (bases, cache directory, system directories, trusted keys, token, allow-unsigned, offline, frozen, the lock path) 'under the fetch module's own names', which the doc names in prose and does not spell per language. LockWrite and Update are the lock's write and update modes of fetch-v1.md §6.

CHS_EXPORT_NONE (-1), the description's export-off constant, at module level; Go types it as Format (ExportNone, its own entry). `export=None` already means no export in Python's Schema.rows, so this is a spelling of the constant, not a second way to call.

Generated from the description by scripts/abi-v1/gen.py: each string vocabulary's decoder from a document's text, with the description's fallback. The decoders use it; §3 names the vocabularies and their facts, not their decoders.

Each artifact class's own code, a class attribute set on every class the binding raises (Python's spelling of one code per class); §4's codes give ArtifactError.code, which every class has, and each binding's CODE_* constants.

Keyword-only constructor parameters of error classes the binding raises: they set §4's refusal fields (reason, path, want, got) and a cache fault's. A caller catches these classes and does not construct them.

The package's implementation modules, public by name. Every public name they hold is re-exported at the top level (measured by this gate: it lists any that is not), and the top level is what the doc describes and the gate compares.

Every format as an array, for iteration: Rust enums cannot be iterated, where Python iterates the IntEnum and TypeScript the const object's values. Not a format: the vocabulary check counts Format's members without it.

A string vocabulary's document spelling. Rust's vocabularies are enums, so the text is a method, where Python's StrEnum member and TypeScript's const-object value are the string itself and Go's type is a string. Generated from the description by scripts/abi-v1/gen.py.
The flag set's raw bits, in and out: Rust's DocFlags is a newtype, where Go's, Python's (IntFlag) and TypeScript's flags are numbers already. Generated from the description by scripts/abi-v1/gen.py.

The five call-error fields from whichever of the four call variants an Error is: Rust's spelling of Go's AsCallError and of catching Python's and TypeScript's CallError base, which §4 names for those languages (for Rust it says 'Rust's match').
Rust's collection idiom (clippy's len_without_is_empty) beside iter() and IntoIterator, which §5 names; Python's ErrorCodeTable has __len__ for the same fact, which the gate treats as protocol.

§3: Rust keeps v0's RawText for every byte output, with the bytes, as_bytes(), as_str() -> Option<&str> and a lossy Display (named in §3's prose, not a table). The rest are its byte-string helpers. The other bindings' byte type is the language's own (string, bytes, Buffer), so they have nothing to name.

§4's 'a cache fault' bullet: a CHTYPES_CACHE_UNUSABLE (fetch-v1.md §1, the cache faults; public issue #486) carries the path, the reason and the errno name, which the doc names in prose and does not spell per language. Rust's variant holds them in its CacheFault struct, as Error::ArtifactCorrupt holds a Refusal.

§3's 'A fact in TypeScript is a free function': TypeScript's vocabularies are const objects (`Format.JSONEachRow` is a number, not an object), which cannot carry a member, so each fact is a free function named for its vocabulary, the language's idiom. An interface since public issue #500, so the gate reads its fields as it reads the other bindings'.

The interface of §4's five call-error fields, which CallError implements and its constructors take: a type-level name for the same fields, so it adds no field. The other bindings spell the fields once, on CallError (Go's struct, Python's class, Rust's struct).

CHS_EXPORT_NONE (-1), the description's export-off constant, as Python spells it (its own entry); Go types it as Format (ExportNone). An absent exportFormat already means no export in TypeScript's RowsOptions.

TypeScript's iteration protocol over the table, beside all(): the counterpart of Rust's IntoIterator, which §5 names. The gate counts TypeScript's [Symbol.dispose] as a name because §2 and §3 name it, so this one is listed rather than treated as protocol.

The ABI v2 dev binding's rule r3 (spec/abi-v2/docs.md): every vocabulary has an unknown(n) member, an unlisted value kept per field, which Go spells as the raw value plus Known() false. docs/reference/bindings-v1.md is the 1.x surface and names none of them; the v2 surface document lands with the other three dev bindings (public issue #511), and this entry goes with it.

The ABI v2 dev binding's rule r3 (spec/abi-v2/docs.md), as Python spells it: an unlisted value of an enum class is that class's unknown(n) member (`Outcome("x")`, named `unknown(x)`), and every vocabulary gains `known`, False for exactly that member (a property on the enum classes, a function on the plain-string Reason and Source); DiscoverQueryParam has `of`, as the other document vocabularies have (their own entry). docs/reference/bindings-v1.md is the 1.x surface and names neither; the v2 surface document lands with the other dev bindings (public issue #511), and this entry goes with it.

The ABI v2 dev binding's rule r3 (spec/abi-v2/docs.md): every vocabulary has an unknown(n) member, an unlisted value kept per field, which TypeScript spells as the raw value (each vocabulary's type is its listed values or Unknown<string | number>) plus a free <vocabulary>Known function, false for it (the same shape as reasonLossy: a const object cannot carry a member); statusName spells an unlisted status unknown(<n>). docs/reference/bindings-v1.md is the 1.x surface and names none of them; the v2 surface document lands with the other dev bindings (public issue #511), and this entry goes with it.

The ABI v2 dev binding's rule r3 (spec/abi-v2/docs.md): every vocabulary has an explicit unknown(n) member, an unlisted value kept per field, which Rust spells as an Unknown variant carrying the raw value, with is_known() false and from_wire/from_code to read one; the call status, the transform reasons and the value sources gain types of their own (Status, Reason, Source; the 1.x status, reason and source modules stay beside them). DiscoverQueryParam.ch_type is the description's ch_type fact of the discovery query's parameters, which Rust alone exposes; the v2 surface document settles it. Refusal.dev_message is rule r6's exact fingerprint message. docs/reference/bindings-v1.md is the 1.x surface and names none of them; the v2 surface document lands with the other dev bindings (public issue #511), and this entry goes with it.
